content.title: How to Watch March Madness 2026: Where to Stream, TV Schedule and Everything to Know
content.text: March Madness is here.A total of 67 games will each be played in the NCAA men’s and women’s Division 1 basketball tournaments (you can see the men’s bracket here and the women’s bracket here). The men’s tournament begins with the First Four, four games played March 17 and 18 in Dayton, Ohio, that feature the four lowest-seeded automatic qualifiers and the four lowest-seeded at-large teams, with the winners advancing to the field of 64.The Final Four will be played April 4 at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. The tournament culminates with a national champion being crowned April 6 at Lucas Oil Stadium.Freshman star Cameron Boozer and Duke earned a No. 1 seed in the men's NCAA basketball tournament. Jared C. Tilton / Getty ImagesThis year’s field features a slew of heavyweights: Duke, Michigan, Arizona and defending champion Florida are among the teams favored to cut down the nets and win it all. What puts the madness in March Madness, though? It’s a little thing known as Cinderella, the term for when a smaller school from a smaller conference manages to beat a favored, more high-profile team, oftentimes breaking people’s brackets.While upsets are part of the magic of this time of year, last year’s tournament featured all four No. 1 seeds making it to the Final Four.On the women’s side, the First Four will be held March 18 and 19 on home courts for the top seeds that will host first-round games. The Final Four is slated to take place at the Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix, with the national championship game played there on April 5. Defending national champion Connecticut, which enters the tournament undefeated, is in a familiar position as the favorite to win its 13th national championship. UCLA, Texas and South Carolina are other threats to to make deep runs.Here’s how to watch this year’s March Madness.How to Watch March Madness 2026MenThe men’s tournament is broadcast among a quartet of networks: truTV, TBS, TNT and CBS. All First Four games will air on truTV.WomenAll of the women’s games will be shown on ESPN’s family of networks.Where Is March Madness Streaming?MenMen’s games can be streamed on HBO Max and Paramount+ (with its premium plan). You can also watch games via free trials available from streaming services Hulu + Live TV, YouTube TV, DirecTV, Sling and Fubo.WomenGames will be available to stream on ESPN’s digital platforms. You can also watch through free trials on Hulu + Live TV, Sling and Fubo. Another viewing option is the Disney+, Hulu, ESPN Unlimited bundle.How to Watch March Madness for FreeMenIn addition to the broadcast options on truTV, TBS, TNT and CBS, you can stream games free of charge on the NCAA March Madness Live app, available on Apple or Google Play.WomenWomen’s games are available on ESPN and ABC and will be streaming on FUBO, which offers a free trial.March Madness 2026 TV ScheduleMenFirst Four: March 17 — truTV. The first game between 16 seeds UMBC and Howard is at 6:40 p.m. ET. Game two between 11 seeds Texas and North Carolina State is scheduled for 9:15 p.m. ET.March 18 — truTV. The first game pitting 16 seeds Lehigh and Prairie View A&M is at 6:40 p.m. ET. Game two between 11 seeds Miami (Ohio) and SMU is scheduled for 9:15 p.m. ET.First round: March 19-20. See the full schedule here. Second round: March 21-22Sweet 16: March 26-27Elite Eight: March 28-29Final Four: April 4 — CBS. The first game is scheduled for 6 p.m. ET, with the second matchup slated to tip off 30 minutes after the first game ends.National championship: April 6 — CBS. The tipoff is scheduled for 8:30 p.m. ET.WomenFirst Four: March 18 — ESPN2. The first game, featuring 11 seeds Richmond and Nebraska, is at 7 p.m. ET. Game two between 16 seeds Stephen F. Austin and Missouri State is scheduled for 9 p.m. ET. March 19 — ESPN2. The first game will match up 16 seeds Samford and Southern at 7 p.m. ET, while game two, scheduled for 9 p.m., has 10 seeds Arizona State and Virginia battling it out.First round: March 20-21. See the full schedule of games. Second round: March 22-23Sweet 16: March 27-28Elite Eight: March 29-30Final Four: April 3 — ESPN. The first of the two semifinals will be played at 7 p.m. ET, with the second contest scheduled for 30 minutes after the first game ends.National championship: April 5 — ABC. The game is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. ET.
